intent: Bring install_usage_monitoring.sh under the 250-line cap by splitting its five steps into a sibling lib/, without changing what the installer does to a machine.
scope: Non-goal: any behaviour change; the trace is the assertion that there is none
Non-goal: wiring the file-length hook, or the pre-existing jscpd venv overage
changes: Moved the five banner-marked sections into lib/ files sourced by the entry script, each wrapped in a named function called in the original order.

REPO_DIR is computed once in the entry script from its own SCRIPT_DIR and read as a global by catchup_timer.sh, rather than recomputed at a lib's directory depth -- recomputing would have silently interpolated the wrong repo root into the generated catch-up script while still exiting 0.

Entry SCRIPT_DIR uses readlink -f on ${BASH_SOURCE[0]} so a symlinked entry point still resolves lib/; the final log line's usage_report.py path is built from that same value so it keeps pointing at bin/, not bin/lib/.
The PKG_* associative arrays stay at lib top level, since `declare -A` inside a function is local and would make every pkg_name lookup return empty.
resolve_and_install_packages ends its bare `[[ -n $clip ]] && pkgs+=(...)` conditional with `|| true` so a false tail cannot become the function's return value under set -e.

Repointed the efficiency test's INSTALLER at lib/nvidia_pmon.sh (which now holds the heredoc it greps) and made its awk extraction anchor whitespace-insensitive, because the repo's pre-commit hook runs `shfmt -w` on staged shell files and rewrites `cat > "x" << 'SCRIPT'` to `cat >"x" <<'SCRIPT'`. All five property assertions are unchanged.

verification.command: meta/scripts/trace_shell_split.sh install_usage_monitoring.sh --prefix /tmp/pfx-before --out /tmp/before.txt (at HEAD, in place at the real repo path)
verification.evidence: exit 0; 11 stubbed calls; 5 files written matching the brief's recorded baseline byte for byte, including usage-report-catchup.sh size=757 sha=9f4803ab157c5527
Empty diff on the post-shfmt split: identical exit status, identical ordered stubbed calls, and all five content hashes unchanged. Each run used a fresh nonexistent prefix.

'Usage monitoring installer efficiency tests passed.' -- all five assertions (no read -t busy-loop, sleeps to day boundary, blocks on wait, printf date builtin, no external date) run against the relocated heredoc.

verification.command: shellcheck + shfmt -d on all seven touched files
verification.evidence: No shellcheck findings and no shfmt diff on any of the seven, after applying shfmt -w so the committed state equals what the pre-commit hook produces.
None of the six files appear in the over-cap list. Line counts: entry 53, catchup_timer 82, nvidia_pmon 89, packages 73, distro_detect 36, system_services 20.

verification.command: jscpd --pattern '**/*.sh' --min-lines 14 --threshold 2, run at HEAD in a clean worktree and again with the split applied
verification.evidence: 27 clones / 1.47% in both cases -- the split adds zero duplication. The 2.51% seen from the main working tree is entirely vendored .venv and .ci-mirror-venv site-packages (tqdm/completion.sh, virtualenv activate.sh), pre-existing and unrelated.
mtimes still May 1 and May 6 2026 after every trace run -- no write escaped the prefix into the live system.

risks: The efficiency test greps a lib's source text, so moving the pmon heredoc again -- or reformatting it -- will break extraction rather than an assertion. The lib header says so and the anchor is now whitespace-tolerant, but a rename of lib/nvidia_pmon.sh still requires updating the test's INSTALLER in the same commit.

REPO_DIR is a global read across a seam. A future lib that shadows it with `local` would change the generated catch-up script's contents while the installer still exits 0; only the trace hash catches that.
The installer was verified under trace stubs, not by a real run against a live machine, so package-manager behaviour on non-Arch families remains as untested as it was before the split.
rollback: git revert the commit; the entry script returns to its 290-line form and lib/ disappears. The generated artifacts on disk are unaffected either way, since neither form was ever executed against the live system here.

After reverting, re-run bash linux_configuration/tests/test_usage_monitoring_installer_efficiency.sh -- it must still print the passed line, since the revert restores both the heredoc location and the original INSTALLER path together.
